Your Memory Dedupe Gate Keeps the Wrong Pairs: Measured on Three Local Encoders

presentation.title_rationale: The selected title frontloads the artifact (memory dedupe threshold) and the exact number a reader would copy (0.95), then states the reader problem as a measured event rather than a universal rule: on this fixture one encoder at 0.95 merged C01, production against staging, at 0.9572. Past tense keeps the claim to what was observed and the body scopes it per encoder and per threshold. The measurement method, the three-encoder design and the year were moved into the description and the introduction, so the headline carries one supported benefit - knowing that a merge gate can lose a live fact - without a 145-character clause chain.
presentation.title_length_note: 61 characters, below the 80-character warning, so no long-title exception is claimed; the research proposal's trailing method and year clauses were relocated, not truncated.
presentation.visual_purpose: The cover shows the one result the article turns on: for each of the three local encoders, the min-to-max range of the 16 paraphrase pairs (blue, should merge) and the 16 critical pairs (red, must not merge), with medians ringed and dashed lines at tau 0.95 and 0.99. On every panel the red bar's top sits above the blue bar's top, which is why no single threshold separates them. Every printed number (0.924/0.993, 0.985/0.998, 0.955/0.992) is the class maximum from summary.json; the image carries no value that is not in the published artifacts and adds no new measurement.
